summary: The pull request's new checks hold where they are pinned, R2-2 is fixed by the key places spec, and the Docs and Version steps pass. Most findings sit where #126's left deferral meets older machinery. A typed defer at a reshape's stop is read as a plan-dial override on the relaunch, a left deferral's task and draft are guarded only by prompts, and three warnings and doc sentences misstate what happens. The rest are two docs that lag the v7 bump or overstate the schema layer, a link check that ignores renamed ids, and a prose-rule call forced only from its tag, which predates the PR. The repository has no scheduled or queued work for these files to overlap.

findings.title: The contract names the unattended section's marker and precheck warning as v6, while the template is v7
findings.description: docs/contract.md:118 says the unattended section carries `<!-- redline-unattended: v6 -->` and quotes the precheck warning as "the plugin ships v6". The template is at v7 (templates/shape-spec-unattended.md:35), and so is this checkout's section (.claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md:26). In the same file, line 175 says v7, and so does docs/upgrading.md:31. This PR moved line 118 from v5 to v6 (96587e3). The v7 bump (4792ca1) updated line 175 and upgrading.md but missed line 118. A reader expects a v6 marker and a "ships v6" warning, while `redline-setup.sh version` reports v7.
findings.proposedFix: On docs/contract.md:118, change both mentions to v7: the marker `<!-- redline-unattended: v7 -->` and the quoted warning "the plugin ships v7".

findings.title: Three texts say the shaper's schema refuses every key it does not name, but a deferred entry accepts any key
findings.description:
Three texts claim the shaper's schema refuses any key it does not name:
- docs/upgrading.md:45: "The shaper's output schema requires the new keys and refuses any key it does not name".
- docs/running.md:86: "the shaper's output schema refuses a key it does not name".
- agents/redline-shaper.md:34, which the shaper itself reads: "the tool you return through refuses a key it does not name, one written a level out included".

A deferred entry is not covered. DEFERRED_SCHEMA (workflows/redline-loop.js:1019-1022) has no `additionalProperties: false`, and that is on purpose: the comment at 1068-1069 says so, and so does the key-places spec (shape.md, decision 21). Of the draft fields, only `fullFix` is required (1021).

The new option shape (995) nests a draft under `draft`. A shaper that nests a deferred entry's draft the same way (`{id, mitigation, fullFix, draft: {title, found, why}}`) passes the schema. checkDrafts (3846-3852) then stops with "the shaper deferred <id> with no drafted issue (missing title, found, why)". That message names no place, while the shaper was told such a key would be refused in its own run, with its path. The resolve agent's schema (1172-1199) is open too, but no text claims otherwise for it.
findings.proposedFix: Narrow the three sentences. The schema refuses an unnamed key on the result, on a finding, inside `cause` and a `swept` entry, and on a call, an option and its `draft`. A deferred entry is open, and the workflow's draft check holds it. Optionally, have checkDrafts say when an entry carries a `draft` key, so the stop names where the fields were found.

findings.title: Deferring a left finding is said to stop the round to show its draft, which never happens under `defer at end`
findings.description:
Two texts say a deferred left finding stops the round to show its draft:
- SKILL.md:213, after a pick of a left call's defer option or a typed `<id>: defer. <reason>`: "Either way the round stops once more to show the draft before it is filed ... with `canFix` false".
- docs/running.md:95: "Either way the round stops once more to show the draft first".

Under `defer at end` no round stops for a draft. `raisesDrafts` is false (workflows/redline-loop.js:4376), so `openDrafts` returns nothing (4401) and `draftStop` never stops (4793-4796). Instead, `holdsDrafts` (4377) holds the draft (5089) for the end-of-run stop, as SKILL.md:262 says for every deferral.

The draft is still shown before it is filed; only the stated time is wrong. The same sentence for any typed defer at SKILL.md:228 predates this pull request. This is R2-1 re-verified at this head; nothing changed it.
findings.proposedFix: In SKILL.md, "Deferring a finding left to the person", and docs/running.md, "Left to you", say the draft is shown before it is filed: at the round's stop, or at the end-of-run stop when deferred items are raised at the end of the run.

findings.title: A typed defer at a reshape's left call is read on the relaunch as a plan-dial override, applied before the finding is left
findings.description:
Since #126, SKILL.md:213 records `<id>: defer. <reason>` for a left finding with `"disposition": "defer"`, at any stop, and the relaunch text (workflows/redline-loop.js:3025) says the same. On origin/main the only call-stop answer that carried a disposition was a decline overrule. SKILL.md:217 refuses that one at a stop after the first resolve, "since the round's first resolve, which ran before it, is where an overrule is applied". Nothing refuses the new typed defer there.

Why it breaks: a reshape can raise a left call. forceAskRules runs on every reshape (vetShape 4332). A reshape whose task for a shaper's fix touches a paths rule, or that tags the finding with a prose rule, forces it and builds a call. That call is `raised` (4899) and the round stops (4917-4921, `afterApproval: true`). On the relaunch the first shape replays, and that shape did not force the finding. `overridesFor(calls)` (4443-4444) counts any decision with a disposition whose id is not among the first shape's calls as a plan-dial override, so the finding joins `overrides`.

What follows:
- `resolve r1` now runs (4797-4799) where the original launch ran none. Its prompt's "Disposition overrides" block (2457-2462) tells the agent to "plan the mitigation the notes describe as a task". The decision carries no `rule`, since `record.forced` is not set yet, so no left-finding bullet applies.
- From that resolve on nothing replays: the plan approver's prompt changes, so it and the reshape rerun as fresh calls.
- If the rerun reshape forces the finding again, it ends left with a draft filed. But `isOverride` (4449) still names it "a disposition override" in any resolve stop (4666), and the first resolve's mitigation task and entry can stand. No workflow check removes them (R3-10).
- If the rerun reshape does not force it, the finding posts as an ordinary decided deferral (outcomesFor 3432). The reply reads `decided by` and drops `left to ... under repository rule`. `decidedAll` marks it overruled (5143, it is in no call), and its mitigation task is built. Under a paths rule the guard refuses a write under the rule's paths; under a prose rule nothing refuses it.

Conditions: guided or plan dial; a plan bounce whose reshape newly puts a finding under a rule (or on one of Redline's own files); the person answers that stop with a typed defer. A pick, or an answer in the person's own words, at the same stop carries no disposition and replays through the reshape (tests/loop-test.mjs:3066-3068 pins this for an own-words answer).

The node harness is refused to the reviewer role, so this is traced through the lines above, not run.
findings.proposedFix: Keep a call stop's answers out of overridesFor. For example, have the skill mark every answer to a call (a `"call": true` key, refused nowhere else) and have overridesFor take only unmarked decisions. Or, at a stop with `afterApproval` true, record a typed defer for a left call without `disposition`, and have resolveWith read it as the defer when the raised call is applied. Add a loop case: a reshape-raised left call answered `R1-1: defer. <reason>` and relaunched. The prompts before the stop must replay, `resolve r1` must not run, and `resolve r1 #1` must carry the decision.

findings.title: A class link to a renamed sibling resolves to the earlier finding that had the old id, with no warning
findings.description:
review() renames every finding whose id lacks this round's prefix (3145-3166) and records each rename in `renamed`. Only the coverage refs follow that map (3220-3238); `sameClassAs` does not. honourLinks runs after the rename (3196). Its test for a link to the same round compares each linked id with the renamed findings (3092), and linkFault (3061-3072) then looks the id up among earlier rounds.

Example: a round-2 reviewer returns findings `R1-1` and `R1-2`, with R1-2's `sameClassAs: ["R1-1"]` meaning its sibling. They become R2-1 and R2-2. 'R1-1' is no finding of this round any more. linkFault finds round 1's R1-1, recorded `fixed`, and the link stands with no warning; the only warnings are the two renames. R2-2 is then shaped as one class with an unrelated earlier finding: the shaper is shown that finding, and checkCauses (3797-3800) stops an `instance` fix for it at `shape`.

Conditions: two reviewer slips together. The reviewer numbers its findings with an earlier round's prefix (the case the rename exists for) and links one of them to a sibling, which its instructions do not ask for. When the misnumbered id was meant as the earlier finding, the same reading is right, so the id is ambiguous rather than always wrong. No pattern in the link-asking schema (889-901) constrains the ids. The node harness is refused to the reviewer role, so this is traced, not run.
findings.proposedFix: In review(), before honourLinks, clear any `sameClassAs` id that is a key of `renamed`, with a warning that it names a finding this review renamed and is ambiguous. Alternatively, map it to the new id, which honourLinks then clears as a finding of this round. Add a loop case with a round-2 review that returns `R1-1` and `R1-2`, the second linked to the first.

findings.title: A call that names a prose rule in why_human but has no askRule tag is applied by Redline as an ordinary call
findings.description:
forceAskRules takes a prose rule only from the shaper's `askRule` tag on the finding (3919-3920). A call whose `why_human` is `repository rule <id>` for a prose rule, on a finding with no tag and no matching paths rule, is never put in `record.forced`. Nothing stops it either:
- the schema's `why_human` enum allows the value (988), and `askRule` is optional (1121);
- checkWhy accepts it as a reason (3607).

The call then runs as an ordinary one. On autopilot, autopilotDecision picks `recommended` (1685-1694) and resolveWith gives the decision that option's end (4516-4518). The recommended change is then planned and built, and its reply reads `decided by: redline (autopilot)` instead of `left to ... under repository rule <id>`. On guided, a pick of an option that ends in `fix` is built the same way. The rules block (670) asks the shaper to set `askRule`; the plan approver's instruction to bounce a task that fixes a prose-covered finding is the only other guard.

This pull request adds two consequences:
- the end is now taken from the option without the resolve agent reading the call;
- a drafted defer option, which OPTIONS_ASK (1161) now asks for on a rule call, is dropped with a warning by checkOptions (3696-3700), since the call is not forced.

The cause predates the pull request: origin/main has the same checkWhy test and the same tag-only lookup. The node harness is refused to the reviewer role, so this is traced through the lines cited, not run.
findings.proposedFix: In forceAskRules, when `s.askRule` is empty, also read a declared rule from the call's `why_human` (`repository rule <id>`) and force the finding under it, with a warning that the tag was missing. Alternatively, make checkWhy stop at `shape` on a rule reason whose finding was not forced. Add a loop case: a prose rule, a call whose why_human names it and whose finding has no tag, on autopilot; it is left to the person.

findings.title: A kept draft's call recommendation doubles a period that ends the draft's title
findings.description: When forceAskRules keeps a shaper's draft as the `Defer to an issue` option, it writes `recommendation: `${DEFER_TO_ISSUE}: ${draftTitle(kept.title)}.``. draftTitle (1618-1621) strips control characters and trims, but leaves a trailing period. The two sibling branches strip one with `.replace(/\.$/, '')` (3939, 3944). So a draft titled "The retry policy is missing." gives "Defer to an issue: The retry policy is missing..". That text is shown in the call, stored as `record.forced[id].recommendation` (3997), and posted in autopilot's Left to line (`open: ...`, 5128). This is R2-3 re-verified at this head; nothing changed it.
findings.proposedFix: Strip a trailing period first: `${DEFER_TO_ISSUE}: ${draftTitle(kept.title).replace(/\.$/, '')}.`. Add a loop case with a period-ended draft title, guided and on autopilot.

findings.title: The unmatched-option warning promises a resolve-agent statement that is never asked for a left finding
findings.proposedFix: Word the warning by case, as the branch at 4527-4534 does. For a forced finding, say the answer is read as the person's own words, so it stays left to the person and nothing is filed. Pin the text with a loop case.

findings.title: A later resolve can replace a left deferral's option draft with no warning
findings.description:
`optionDraft` is built only for the ids this resolve applies (4605). `returned` admits an entry for any `leftDeferred` id (4615), including one that an earlier resolve in the round applied.

Example: the round's first resolve applies R1-1, a left finding the person deferred by picking its drafted option. A later resolve, set off by a reshape's raised call (4923-4926), returns an entry for R1-1 too:
- the entry gets no `rewritten` warning (4616-4619), since that check reads `optionDraft` only;
- `stated` has no entry for a forced id, so it is no `strayCall` (4650) and passes into `fresh`;
- it replaces the option's draft in `deferred` (4727).

That breaks the rule in the comment at 4597-4603: the option's draft is filed, because the person was shown it. On a dial that raises drafts, draftsOf bumps the version (4396-4397), and the person is shown version 2 with no note that it differs from the option they picked. Under `defer at end`, the rewritten draft is the one held and shown.

Conditions: the later resolve returns an entry for a finding its prompt does not name (resolvePrompt's `callDecisions` holds only the raised calls, 2400). This is R2-5 re-verified at this head.
findings.proposedFix: Build `optionDraft` for every left deferral of the round that has a recorded option draft, not only for `applied`. Or drop, with a warning, a returned entry for a left id this resolve did not apply, so the earlier entry stands.

findings.title: No workflow check keeps a left deferral's mitigation and task empty when its call offered no draft
findings.proposedFix: In resolveWith, set `mitigation: ''` on every kept deferred entry whose id is in `record.forced`, and do the same where a reshape rebuilds `deferred` (4916). Throw a checkError at `resolve` when `taskFiles(id)` is not empty for a forced id it applies: "the resolve agent planned a task with files for <id>, a finding left to the person under <rule>; no task writes anything for it". Add loop cases for both paths: a picked undrafted Mitigate option of a relabelled call, and a typed defer on a call with no draft, each with a resolve that returns a mitigation and a task with files.

findings.title: For a left deferral with a commit of its own, the warning gives a false reason and implies a reply names the commit
findings.description:
Since #126, isDeferral returns true for a left deferral (4771-4774), so `roundDeferred` and `roundDeferrals` include it (5001, 5088). It therefore reaches the warning loop that compares a deferral's own commit with its plan (5101-5114).

For a forced id, `plannedFiles` takes `shaperFiles` (4757), because `tracked` is false. shaperFiles reads only a finding the shaper sorted as defer (4386-4389), and a forced finding is `ask`, so the list is always empty. A commit whose subject opens with the finding's id therefore gives "<id> has a commit of its own (<sha>) and the resolve agent planned no task with files for it; posted with its decision" (5112-5113).

The reason is false whenever the resolve agent did plan files (`decidedFiles[id]`, 4724-4726). The comment above the warning, "The commit is the record, so it counts" (5107-5110), does not hold here either: outcomesFor's left branch sets `commits: []` (3427), so neither the reply nor the handoff names the commit. Reaching this needs a commit for a finding left under a rule, the path R3-10 leaves open. This is R2-7 re-verified at this head.
findings.proposedFix: In the loop at 5101-5114, read `decidedFiles[id]` for a forced id, and say that the commit is not reported because the finding is left to the person under its rule. Or, with R3-10's resolve check in place, warn on any commit of a left finding's own as written under the rule.

list.summary: Typing `<id>: defer. <reason>` on a left finding at the stop a reshape's raised call makes is read on the relaunch as a disposition override from the plan dial, not as that call's decision. `overridesFor(calls)` treats any decision with a `disposition` whose id is not among the first shape's calls as an override, and a raised call is never among them. #126 made SKILL.md record exactly this answer with `"disposition": "defer"`; before it, no call answer carried a disposition. Fix: keep a raised call's decision out of the first resolve's overrides, for example by marking a decision taken at a call stop as a call's, or by limiting overrides to findings the first shape sorted fix, decline or defer whose id no reshape raises.
list.failure_scenario: Round 1's first shape sorts R1-5 as fix, and no rule covers it. The plan bounces, and the reshape's task for R1-5 touches config/project/**, a paths rule, so forceAskRules builds a left call and the run stops for it. The person types `R1-5: defer. track it`, recorded as {choice: defer, disposition: defer}. On the relaunch shape r1 replays, but overridesFor(calls) returns R1-5. The first resolve now runs with an override block it did not have, telling the agent to plan the mitigation as a task for a finding that is not yet forced. From that resolve on nothing replays: the plan approvers and the reshape all rerun. The agent may plan a mitigation task under the rule's path. If the rerun reshape does not force R1-5 again, the left deferral is filed and posted as an ordinary decided deferral (a 'decided by' reply, not 'left to @x under repository rule'), and the warnings call it 'a disposition override'.

list.summary: A call that reads as left under a prose repository rule is applied by Redline when the shaper names the rule only in `why_human` and not in `askRule` on the finding. forceAskRules takes a prose rule only from the finding's `askRule` tag. checkWhy accepts `repository rule <id>` as a reason, so the call goes through and is never recorded in `record.forced`. With #105 an autopilot pick then takes its option's end as the disposition, and #126's checkOptions drops the drafted issue on its defer option with a warning. Fix: when `s.askRule` is empty, also take the declared rule from the call's `why_human`, or make checkWhy stop on a rule reason whose finding was not forced.
list.failure_scenario: A repository declares the prose rule `schema-change`. The shaper returns R1-2 as ask with a call whose why_human is 'repository rule schema-change', but leaves askRule off the finding, and no paths rule matches. forceAskRules finds no rule and checkWhy passes. On autopilot, autopilotDecision picks the recommended 'Change it' (ends fix), resolveWith sets disposition fix, and the implementer builds a change the rule says a person makes. The thread gets a decided reply, not 'left to @x under repository rule'.

list.summary: A class link can be kept against an unrelated earlier finding with no warning. honourLinks's same-round test compares each sameClassAs id with the findings after review() renumbers them, but the rename map built at 3147-3165 is never applied to sameClassAs. When a reviewer misnumbers its findings with the previous round's prefix, a link to its own sibling then resolves to the earlier round's finding of that id. Fix: when a link id is one the reviewer used for a finding the workflow renamed (a key of `renamed`), clear it with a warning that it is ambiguous instead of resolving it against the earlier rounds.
list.failure_scenario: The round 2 reviewer returns findings 'R1-1' and 'R1-2', with R1-2's sameClassAs ['R1-1'] meaning its sibling. They are renamed R2-1 and R2-2. honourLinks does not see 'R1-1' as a finding of this round, and linkFault finds round 1's R1-1, which was fixed, so the link stands silently. R2-2 is shaped as a class of an unrelated earlier finding, and checkCauses stops an instance fix at shape.

list.summary: The contract states the wrong current version of the unattended section. It says the marker is `<!-- redline-unattended: v6 -->` and quotes the precheck warning as 'the plugin ships v6', but templates/shape-spec-unattended.md and this checkout's shape-spec.md are v7. Commit 4792ca1 bumped line 175 and docs/upgrading.md to v7 and missed this line, which the branch had already moved from v5 to v6. Fix: change both mentions on line 118 to v7.
list.failure_scenario: A reader of docs/contract.md expects a v6 marker and a 'ships v6' warning, while `redline-setup.sh version` reports v7.

list.summary: The docs say the shaper's output schema refuses any key it does not name, but deferred entries stay open. DEFERRED_SCHEMA (workflows/redline-loop.js:1019-1022) has no `additionalProperties: false`, which the key-places spec keeps on purpose (decision 21). docs/running.md:86 and agents/redline-shaper.md:34, a claim the shaper itself is shown, say the same. A deferred entry that nests its draft fields under `draft`, the shape the new options use, is accepted while fullFix sits at the top level, then stops at checkDrafts naming no place. Fix: narrow the claim to the result, findings, cause, calls, options and their drafts, and say a deferred entry is held by the workflow's own draft check.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper returns deferred [{id: 'R1-4', mitigation: '', fullFix: '...', draft: {title, found, why}}]. The schema accepts it, and checkDrafts stops with 'missing title, found, why', with no hint that they sit under draft. The shaper was told such a key would be refused in its own run with its path.
